args.text: [lane-ibis] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: if a service moves, users are sent to the old, dead or wrong server. (2) Slow recovery: failover and emergency changes take longer to reach users, extending outages. (3) Poisoned answers linger: if a forged answer is cached, the harm lasts until it expires.

[lane-ibis] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether a request was processed, and retrying is the only safe way to recover. If the operation is idempotent (repeating it gives the same result as doing it once), a retry cannot cause duplicate charges, records or messages.

[lane-ibis] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) Size: it takes 16 bytes, which is larger than a typical 4 or 8 byte integer, so indexes and foreign keys use more space. (2) Leaked timing: the leading bits hold a timestamp, so anyone seeing an ID can estimate when the record was created, and IDs made in the same millisecond may not sort in strict creation order.

[lane-ibis] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before applying it to the main data files. If the system crashes, it replays the log to restore a consistent state, so committed work is not lost and half-finished changes can be undone.

[lane-ibis] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a newer client may change speed through its own tuning, so an unpinned version can make results differ for reasons unrelated to what is being tested. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the same setup later and get comparable numbers, because the client code does not change underneath the test.
